failure_analysis.what_failed: On the sine scenarios the supervisor over-shifts the split toward high h1 / low h2. The pump-gain estimate uses the last sample only, k = f4/(0.8*v1), which is biased LOW whenever the voltage moves faster than tank4 can follow (PI overshoot or the 12 V limit): the measured h4-flow lags the pump voltage, so the code thinks pump 1 is weak. The predicted voltage for every candidate is then inflated, and the 2000 V^-1 saturation penalty dominates the 3000 m^-1 upper-level and band penalties, forcing splits that drive h2 below 0.25 m and h3 above 0.75 m (dev_feed_sine_2: 272 s band, 123 s upper, 1.11 m travel; dev_pump_sine_0 and dev_combined_sine_1 show the same over-shift signature).
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: With the gain bias gone, re-examine the residual sine losses: the load residual (d1,d2) is still polluted by the tank level rates and by the supervisor's own transients, so a persistence/validity gate on the load estimate is the next candidate, not an averaging filter.

self_check: The pump-gain estimate is now the accumulation-corrected flow ratio (f4 + dh4/dt)/(0.8*v1) averaged over 30 s, which is an exact consequence of tank4's mass balance, so it is unbiased even while a pump saturates or the PI loop overshoots its new steady voltage. When a disturbance drives an upper level or a pump toward its limit, the candidate split is therefore scored with the true voltage requirement, and the supervisor shifts the split only as far as needed to keep h2 inside its band and h3/h4 below the limit instead of over-shifting and dragging h2 out of band. Production stays on target because every candidate keeps q1+q2 = Q exactly, so once the loops settle at any feasible split the reported Q equals the target.
proposed_change: Replace the single-sample pump-gain estimate (f4/v1 with a min) by the accumulation-corrected ratio (f4 + dh4/dt)/(0.8*v1) averaged over the last 30 samples, for both pumps.
reason: beat the champion but candidate 2 scored lower

failure_analysis.what_failed: The oscillating-disturbance scenarios dominate the battery (feed mean 388.9, combined 222.2). The split is chosen from the instantaneous mass-balance load, but that estimate equals the true load minus the tank's own level rate, so it lags a swinging disturbance by tens of seconds; the supervisor's own 45 s post-move hold adds a second delay. The h1/h2 bias is therefore applied late in each cycle: the loops saturate (v1 = 12 V in the feed2 troughs) or push v2/h3 up (h3 = 0.85 m at the feed2 crests), so the actual levels leave the constant-Q curve (Q errors up to 1.7 L/s) while h2 drops out of its band and h3 exceeds its limit.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: Tune only the two scalar parameters of the new lead (80 s horizon, 1.5 L/s clamp) if travel on step/ramp scenarios grows; do not additionally average or filter the load, since the flat-mean attempts (gen1 c1-c3, gen2 c2-c3) destroyed the sine response.

self_check: The split is now chosen for the load that is about to act, not the load that just acted: in a feed2 trough the predicted (more negative) load makes the optimizer move production to tank1 early, so pump 1 is not held at 12 V, h2 stays in its band and the actual pair stays on the constant-Q curve; towards a crest the predicted high load makes the h3 prediction exceed its target early, so h1 is held back and v2/h3 stay under their limits. The extrapolation is bounded to +/-1.5 L/s and the correction term (level rate) keeps the trend meaningful during the supervisor's own transients, so a step or ramp cannot trigger a runaway split; the existing travel penalty, 45 s hold and 0.06 m/call rate limit still cap setpoint motion. If the trend is wrong the error is at most about 0.05 m of h2 bias, which the soft constraint weights absorb.
proposed_change: Replace the instantaneous load used for the split decision with a lead-compensated load: the accumulation-corrected (level-rate-corrected) estimate is differenced over the last 60 s and extrapolated 80 s ahead, clamped to +/-1.5 L/s, so the setpoint bias leads a swinging disturbance instead of trailing it.

failure_analysis.what_failed: Oscillating disturbances dominate the battery (dev_feed_sine_2 1659, dev_feed_sine_1 872, dev_combined_sine_1 872, dev_pump_sine_0 535, dev_split_sine_1 402). During a sine the upper tanks fill and drain (large dh3/dt, dh4/dt), but the code derives the pump-flow estimate for the gain check from the steady-state relation Am=f4/0.8, Bm=f3/0.8. At t~1040 s of dev_feed_sine_2 this makes k1e read 0.00065 instead of 0.00085 (a fake 24% pump loss). The split optimizer then believes pump 1 is weak, so it shifts production onto pump 2 (h1 up, h2 down), which saturates v1 at 12 V, drives h3 above 0.75 m (123 s) and pushes h2 below its band (272 s), while Q sits 1-2 L/s off target.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: If the corrected gains are not enough, next test a short 30-60 s mean of the accumulation-corrected pump flow, which removes the residual oscillation-driven gain bias without freezing the split response.

self_check: The split optimizer keeps its steady-state cost function, but the pump-flow inputs that set k1e and k2e now come from the upper-tank mass balance (outflow plus the measured level rate), so a transient fill or drain of tank3/tank4 is no longer mistaken for a 20-30% pump-gain loss. Because the model no longer believes a pump is weak, it stops shifting production onto the other pump, which keeps h3/h4 below the 0.75 m limit and keeps both voltages away from the 12 V rail instead of pinning one at saturation. The load term d1,d2 stays instantaneous, so the split still moves enough to keep h2 inside its band and Q on target during a real feed/pump/split disturbance, and the 0.06 m per call rate limit still caps the setpoint travel.
proposed_change: Compute the pump-flow estimates used for the gain estimates k1e and k2e from the upper-tank mass balance including the measured level rates, (f4+dh4/dt)/(1-gam1) and (f3+dh3/dt)/(1-gam2), while leaving the load estimate d1,d2 on the original static flows.

failure_analysis.what_failed: The supervisor chose setpoints by inverting the steady-state mass balances, implicitly assuming the PI loops sit exactly on their setpoints. When a feed/pump/split disturbance swings, the loops hold a proportional offset (e.g. h2 measured 0.44 m with setpoint 0.35 m, or 0.20 m with setpoint 0.30 m), so the levels actually achieved are setpoint+offset: produced Q swings by +-0.7-0.9 L/s (749 L off target on dev_feed_sine_2, 544 L on dev_feed_sine_1) and the achieved h2 leaves its band for 180-280 s, while the setpoint moves chosen by the split optimiser never aimed at the achieved level.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: If this promotes, next look at the split-optimiser weights (3000 constraint vs 200 travel) and whether the upper-level prediction h3p/h4p should use measured accumulation, since combined_sine_0 still shows h3 above the limit.

self_check: Every candidate split is now scored on the levels and pump flows the plant will actually reach: the commanded setpoint is the desired achieved level minus the measured PI tracking offset (clamped to 0.12 m), so a swinging disturbance that leaves the loops lagging is compensated instead of being taken for the desired operating point. Because the achieved h2 is what enters the band cost, and the achieved production is pinned to the target by construction (q1+q2=target on achieved levels), both the production error and the h2 band excursions shrink. Pump saturation (predicted v1p or v2p above 12 V) and the upper-level limit are penalised in the same cost, so the split shifts production to the unloaded tank and keeps predicted h3/h4 below ulim-0.05; the offset clamp and the h2 setpoint clamp at h2_band+-0.05 keep the compensation from ever driving the setpoints wild.
proposed_change: Evaluate every candidate split on the levels the PI loops will actually achieve (setpoint plus the measured tracking offset off1=h1-sp_h1, off2=h2-sp_h2, clamped to +-0.12 m) and command setpoint = achieved_level - offset, instead of assuming the loops sit on their setpoints.

failure_analysis.what_failed: In the split optimizer the only voltage cost is the 2000-per-volt penalty above vmax=12 V, so whenever a disturbance pushes a pump the optimizer parks the demanded voltage right at the boundary (trace dev_feed_sine_2, t=460 s: chosen pair gives v1p=11.98 V while real v1=12.0 V is already saturated). With zero headroom the very next half-cycle of the feed oscillation saturates pump 1, the h2 loop loses authority, h2 dives to 0.204 m (below the 0.25 band) for 277 s and Q falls to 14.7 L/s, so both the band and the production objectives fail on the oscillating scenarios.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: Keep the voltage-margin mechanism and tune its size (margin and slope) on the oscillation scenarios; do not go back to filtering/averaging the load, which measurably loses on dev_feed_sine because it removes the in-phase correction that keeps h2 alive.

self_check: The split optimizer now prices predicted pump voltage above 11 V (12 V minus a 1 V margin) with a 700-per-volt slope on top of the existing hard 2000-per-volt penalty above 12 V, so it never parks a pump at the saturation boundary. When a disturbance would demand, say, 11.98 V from the tank2 chain, the extra cost makes the optimizer move production toward tank1 (h1 up, h2 down) until the predicted voltage is back inside the margin and the level the pump holds is achievable. That keeps the demanded h2 setpoint feasible, so h2 stays inside [0.25, 0.45], and it keeps 0.8*k1*v1 plus the tank4 drain able to supply the tank2 draw-off, so Q stays on target instead of collapsing when the pump saturates. The margin costs nothing at the nominal point (v1=9.0 V, v2=9.16 V), so steady operation and the production-target tracking are unchanged.
proposed_change: Add a soft 700-per-volt penalty on the predicted pump voltages above vmax-1.0 V in the setpoint-split cost, so the optimizer keeps a one-volt saturation margin instead of parking a pump at the 12 V limit.

failure_analysis.what_failed: The sine/oscillating scenarios dominate the battery (production off target is 77% of the score, band seconds 16%). In the two worst traces (dev_feed_sine_2, dev_feed_sine_1) a +/-2.5 L/s feed2 oscillation swings h2 by about +/-0.12 m with a ~360 s period. The supervisor's split bias is computed from the load estimate d1,d2 built on the upper-tank outflows f3,f4; during a swing the upper tanks store flow (dh4/dt + 0.25*dh3/dt appears in the residual), so the estimate lags the true load by the upper tank's storage time constant (~100 s). At each half-cycle the supervisor therefore keeps h2's setpoint high and h1 low (e.g. sp=[0.269,0.391] while the true draw-off is -2.46 L/s) exactly while the tank-2 loop is already saturated at v1=12 V; h2 then sits at 0.19-0.21 m, below the 0.25 band low, and Q runs about 1.5 L/s below target. The correct pair at that instant (h1~0.33, h2~0.31 with v1~12.0 V) is never commanded, so both the production integral and the band seconds grow; h3 also stays within 0.07 m of 0.75, so any extra tank-1 production must be headroom-limited.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: Keep the bounded measured-production feedback and, if it promotes, add the symmetric trim in the 'too little production' case via h2 restrained by the tank-4/v1 headroom; do not go back to level-derivative or low-pass load estimates, both measured worse than the lagged static estimate.

self_check: When the measured production is short the trim raises only the tank-1 setpoint, which raises pump 2, so the extra pump-2 flow (4/3 of the trim) is explicitly bounded by the tank-3 headroom: the guard compares the predicted pump-2 flow and the flow implied by the measured h3 against the flow that drives h3 to ulim-0.10, and simply refuses the upward trim when there is no room. The downward trim (production too high) is never blocked because it lowers pump 2 and h3, and it also pulls h2 down, which is what the band needs during the overshooting half-cycle. Both directions are hard-limited to 0.02 m of h1 and 0.4 L/s of flow, so the trim cannot dominate the model split, cannot drive a pump further into saturation (it lowers pump 1 by 1/3 of the trim when positive), and vanishes at steady state because the model pair is already on the constant-Q curve.
proposed_change: Add a bounded, measured-production-error feedback trim on the tank-1 setpoint (bounded by the tank-3/pump-2 headroom) so the split compensates the production error in phase with the actual error instead of relying only on the ~100 s-lagged load estimate.

failure_analysis.what_failed: Oscillatory (sine) disturbances dominate the battery: dev_feed_sine_2/1/0 and dev_combined_sine_1/0 lose almost all their points on 'production off target' (776, 520, 361, 361, 237 L) plus 292/146/161/68 s of h2 outside its band. The traces show why the h1 handle cannot keep up: with a ~340 s sine on tank2, h2 is pushed to 0.45 (loop driving v1 to ~3 V) on the inflow half and to ~0.20 with v1 saturated at 12 V on the draw-off half, so q2 swings by +-1 L/s and h1 must swing about +-0.08 m (+-0.16 m per half cycle). The supervisor's h1 setpoint only moves ~0.08 m per half cycle (sp_h1 goes 0.266 -> 0.348) because the only production feedback is the measured-production trim, and that trim is rate-starved: the 45 s post-setpoint-change hold lets it act once per ~50 s and its step is hard-capped at 0.02 m and 0.4 L/s, i.e. an effective slew of 0.4 mm/s against the 1.5 mm/s the sine demands, leaving a standing +-1 L/s error that is in phase but a quarter period late. The constraint-driven split itself is fine (it tracks the h3 headroom and h2 band) but it does not remove the production error created by the h2 loop's own tracking shortfall, and in the draw-off half the tank-3 headroom guard blocks the upward trim entirely, so the whole correction must come from the (rate-limited) trim.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: The upward trim in the draw-off half is repeatedly blocked because Bcur=max(f3/0.8, best_Bp) already sits at the ulim-0.10 tank-3 target, while the measured h3 only reaches ~0.66 m; a follow-up should replace the fixed -0.10 m margin with a measured-headroom term (or raise it to -0.03 m) once this trim retune is shown not to push h3 over the limit.

self_check: The trim is now the fast outer production loop: every call it converts the measured production error directly into an h1 setpoint move (gain 0.8, hard limits 1.2e-3 m3/s and 0.05 m), so when a sine load makes h2 sit above or below its setpoint, q1 is corrected within one or two calls instead of one step per 50 s hold period. The same trim is self-limiting on the dangerous side: the upward move is refused once the pump-2 flow implied by the measured h3 (or by the predicted split) reaches the flow that puts tank 3 at ulim-0.10, so lifting h1 can never drive h3 over its limit, while the downward move is always safe because it unloads pump 2 and tank 3. Because the trim only touches h1 (the split's production handle) and never h2 or the pump voltages, and its step is capped, it cannot push a saturated pump further: when v1 or v2 is at 12 V the correction still comes from the h1 side, which is exactly the free degree of freedom. The constraint-driven split keeps its original 45 s hold so it still ignores its own setpoint transient; only the measured-production correction runs every call.
proposed_change: Retune the measured-production trim into the fast outer loop: it now runs on every call (the 45 s post-change hold freezes only the constraint-driven split) with gain 0.8 instead of 0.30 and step caps of 1.2e-3 m3/s and 0.05 m instead of 4.0e-4 and 0.02 m, so h1 tracks a swinging load instead of stepping once per hold period.

failure_analysis.what_failed: In the sinusoidal feed scenarios the supervisor's own split swing, not the disturbance alone, drives the score. The split cost judges the h3/h4 level limits on the INSTANTANEOUS load residual, but tank3/tank4 are slow states (tau about 100-175 s) that cannot follow a 350 s load swing, so the predicted h3 (0.71-0.78 m) is far above the plant's h3 (0.62-0.67 m). The guard therefore over-shifts the split (h2 setpoint to 0.385-0.397 m, near the band top) at every positive half-cycle. Two consequences: (a) the h2 loop needs an offset of about d2/((1-g1)k1Kp) = 0.06-0.12 m to push flow against the load, so with the h2 setpoint parked high the level exceeds 0.45 m, and (b) when the load reverses the same high setpoint demands v1 = 13.6 V, pump 1 saturates, h2 collapses to 0.194-0.242 m and production falls about 1.5 L/s short for 100 s or more. The counterweight is that the pump-voltage limits are genuinely instantaneous, so they must keep using the unsmoothed load.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: If this is promoted, next look at the nominal target-change group: 0.19-0.30 m of travel against about 0.08-0.15 m of ideal travel suggests the measured-production trim (gain 0.3, clamp 0.02 m) is limit-cycling the h1 setpoint off the Q = target manifold during the 100 s loop transient.

self_check: The split is still solved on the instantaneous mass balance for the pump voltages, so a pump that would saturate at 12 V or a real step load still shifts production to the other tank immediately, and the production-error trim still closes any residual Q error. What changed is only the h3/h4 limit check: it now uses the load smoothed with the upper tanks' own storage time constant (100 s), because a half-cycle of a fast load swing never reaches those tanks, and judging it on the instantaneous load over-predicted h3, over-shifted the split and parked the h2 setpoint at the top of its band. With the h2 setpoint kept nearer the band centre, the h2 loop's unavoidable load excursion stays inside [0.25, 0.45] instead of breaking it, and the setpoints still move only when a constraint is actually predicted to be violated, through the same movement cost and 0.06 m step limit.
proposed_change: Judge the slow h3/h4 upper-level limits on a load residual smoothed over the upper tanks' storage time constant (tau = 100 s) while keeping the instantaneous load for the production split and the pump-voltage limits.

failure_analysis.what_failed: The worst scenarios are the swinging-disturbance ones (dev_feed_sine_2 1440, dev_feed_sine_1 860, dev_combined_sine_1 709, dev_combined_sine_0 524). In those traces the tank2 feed swing saturates pump 1 (v1 pinned at 12 V for ~100 s per trough), so the h2 loop cannot hold its level and production sits ~1.5 L/s low, while the h1 setpoint is pushed up only once the trough has already arrived (t=490 vs the d2 minimum at t=460-480). The load-driven split is in phase with the disturbance, but the production-error trim that is supposed to finish the job is purely proportional, and a setpoint change needs 1.5-2 min to reach the product, so the production correction lands about a half-cycle late and the surplus half-cycle (+0.7-0.9 L/s) is also left uncorrected.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: If the lag-compensated trim still leaves trough error, feed the measured pump saturation (v1 or v2 near 12 V with the level off its setpoint) into the split choice itself, not just into the trim, because the tank-4-to-tank2 fill lag is what starvation looks like in the measurements.

self_check: The change only alters the signal the production trim acts on: it predicts the production error one plant lag ahead from its own 90 s slope, and the prediction is never allowed to reverse the sign of the error actually measured, so a step or target change can only be corrected faster, never in the wrong direction. Every increment stays inside the old bounds (gain 0.30, |dq1| <= 0.4 L/s, |dh1| <= 0.02 m) and the upward push is still refused once the predicted pump-2 flow has already brought tank 3 to ulim - 0.10, so when a pump saturates the re-split of production toward tank1 is limited by tank-3 headroom and no upper level is driven over its limit. Production therefore recovers toward target at the fastest rate the remaining loop and headroom allow, and when a pump is pinned the trim simply stops adding instead of pushing tank 3 past its limit.
proposed_change: Replace the instantaneous production error in the tank-1 trim with a lag-compensated (PD) production error, eq + 80 s * (slope of eq over the last 90 s), clamped and sign-guarded so it may only reinforce the measured error, never reverse it.

failure_analysis.what_failed: The battery is dominated by the multi-minute feed2 sine scenarios: the production trim acts on the measured production error, and with the 90 s backward-difference slope its correction reaches the product about half a cycle (~175 s) late, so the tank-1 split correction arrives in anti-phase, amplifies the swing (Q swings grow from 16.97/14.75 to 17.15/14.66 over the run) and lets pump 1 sit at 12 V while h2 sinks to 0.21 m. The same lag is what makes all the dev_*_sine_* scenarios score 3-10x the step/ramp ones.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: If the re-timed trim is promoted, next attack the split's own lag: the load used for the split is inferred from the tank-4 outflow, so the tank-2 imbalance that saturates pump 1 is seen ~100 s late; add the measured lower-tank level rate only inside a pump-saturation gate.

self_check: The change only re-times the production-error trim: its sign guard, its 2.5e-3 m3/s / 4e-4 m3/s / 0.02 m clamps and the tank-3 headroom bound (h3 <= ulim-0.10) are untouched, so as soon as h3 nears its limit the upward h1 trim is zeroed and the split stays inside the upper-level guard. The split itself still comes from the constrained candidate scan, which penalizes predicted h3/h4 above ulim-0.05 and predicted v1/v2 above 12 V, so a saturating pump or a rising upper level shifts production to the other tank instead of asking for flow that pump cannot deliver. Because the predictor is unchanged for a steady ramp (the same 80 s of lead at the same slope), step and ramp scenarios keep the previous behaviour and only the oscillatory response is re-phased.
proposed_change: Shrink the slope window of the lag-compensated production trim from 90 s to 30 s while keeping the 80 s prediction horizon, so the predictor actually delivers its intended phase lead instead of losing 45 s to the long backward difference.

failure_analysis.what_failed: The lagged/optimistic load estimate makes the constraint-driven split ask pump 1 (the h2 loop's actuator) for more flow than it can give: in the feed-sine scenarios v1 pins at 12 V for ~1-2 min per half cycle while h2 is still 0.10-0.17 m below its setpoint, so h2 leaves the band, drops to ~0.21 m and production falls 1.5 L/s short for a long time; the split only reacts when the ~55-90 s lagged residual estimate crosses a threshold, i.e. about a quarter cycle late.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: Keep the saturation relief as the split's fast inner guard and, if more gain is needed, add a matching release/settle logic that returns h2 to the split optimum once the sustained-flow reversal (h2 rising while v1 is still high) is observed, rather than relying on the lagged load estimate to un-ratchet it.

self_check: The split optimization still chooses production shares from the load model, but when a measured pump voltage sits on its ceiling while that pump's own tank level is short of the commanded setpoint and not rising, the commanded split is demonstrably unachievable, so the code shifts a fixed 0.5 L/s of production from that pump's tank to the other one, holding total production constant by construction and clamping the h2 share to its band. The lag-compensated production trim then keeps Q on target, and the shift is refused whenever the model predicts the shifted pair would push h3 or h4 past the limit, so an upper level cannot be traded for pump headroom. Because the trigger is the clamped voltage plus a non-rising level error, a voltage overshoot from the supervisor's own setpoint change cannot fire it, and the shift stops by itself once the pump comes off the ceiling.
proposed_change: Add a pump-saturation relief on the split: when a measured pump voltage is at its ceiling while that pump's lower-tank level is still below the commanded setpoint and not rising, shift 0.5 L/s of production from that pump's tank to the other tank (production preserved, h2 clamped to its band and the shift rejected if the model predicts an upper level above the limit).
reason: beat the champion but candidate 1 scored lower

failure_analysis.what_failed: The sine-disturbance scenarios (dev_feed_sine_2 1399.7, dev_feed_sine_1 874.8, dev_combined_sine_0 531.7) dominate the battery: with a +-2.45 L/s feed2 swing the draw-off half pushes pump 1 to its 12 V limit, tank 4 is drained by the loop during the inflow half, and h2 sags below the 0.25 m band for 153-277 s while production runs ~1.5 L/s low at each trough (525-768 L off target). The decision traces show the split only advances every ~50 s (sp changes at 480, 530, 580, 630, 680, 730 ... s in feed_sine_2) - exactly the 45 s post-setpoint-change hold, which freezes both the model-based split and the measured-production trim for 4-5 calls after every own move, so in a 350-400 s oscillation the compensation is staircased and arrives about a half cycle late. The earlier experiment that lengthened this hold to 100 s made every type mean worse (feed 356 -> 560, pump 121 -> 205, split 131 -> 150, nominal 239 -> 253), confirming that the hold length is the dominant lag, not a protective optimum.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: Keep the shortened hold and re-check the sine scenarios; if the shorter hold still leaves a half-cycle lag, add a phase lead on the h2 setpoint (pre-charge tank 4 during the inflow half) rather than touching the load/gain estimators again.

self_check: Shortening the own-transient hold from 45 s to 25 s makes the supervisor re-plan the split about every 25 s instead of every 50 s, so the production trim and the model split follow the swing of a several-minute disturbance instead of staircasing behind it, which cuts the integrated production error and shortens the time h2 spends under its band. The model-based split is unchanged: every candidate pair is still scored with the predicted tank-3/tank-4 heads and the predicted pump voltages, so when a pump approaches saturation the split is shifted toward the other pump while h3 and h4 are kept below their limit, and the production trim is still bounded by the tank-3 headroom guard so a raise of h1 can never push h3 into its limit. The hold is not removed, only shortened, so the first (most corrupted) samples of our own setpoint transient are still skipped before the mass-balance residual is trusted again.
proposed_change: Reduce the fixed 'recent own setpoint change' hold from 45 s to 25 s so the split is not staircased at ~50 s and can track a several-minute load swing (and complete a multi-step target move) without changing any estimator, guard or cost.
